description:
Naye Fal Bagicho Ki Sthapana is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India aimed at promoting horticulture and enhancing the livelihoods of farmers across the country. 

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2021. 

It was introduced as part of the larger National Horticulture Mission which was first initiated in 2005. 

The primary objective of Naye Fal Bagicho Ki Sthapana is to create new orchards and enhance the production of fruits in various regions of India. 

The scheme aims to increase the area under fruit cultivation by 10 percent by the year 2025. 

It also targets to improve the income of farmers engaged in horticulture by at least 20 percent over the next five years. 

The initiative is designed to provide financial assistance and technical support to farmers who wish to establish new orchards. 

Under this scheme, farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh per hectare for the establishment of new orchards. 

The assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy which covers 50 percent of the total cost incurred by the farmer. 

The scheme also encourages the cultivation of high-yielding and disease-resistant fruit varieties. 

Farmers are provided with training and guidance on best practices for orchard management. 

The scheme emphasizes the importance of sustainable agricultural practices to ensure long-term productivity. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on small and marginal farmers. 

Farmers must possess a minimum of 0.5 hectares of land to qualify for the assistance. 

The annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 2 lakh to be eligible for the benefits of the scheme. 

The scheme is open to all farmers regardless of their educational background. 

However, preference is given to farmers who have undergone training in horticulture or related fields. 

To apply for the Naye Fal Bagicho Ki Sthapana scheme, farmers must follow a specific application process. 

The first step is to obtain the application form from the local agricultural office or the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

Farmers must fill out the application form with accurate details regarding their land and farming practices. 

Along with the application form, farmers are required to submit documents such as land ownership proof, identity proof, and income certificate. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local agricultural officer. 

The officer conducts a field visit to verify the details provided in the application. 

If the application is approved, the farmer receives a sanction letter detailing the subsidy amount. 

The funds are disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The disbursement typically occurs within 30 days of the approval of the application. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Horticulture in each state. 

State governments are responsible for the execution and monitoring of the scheme at the ground level. 

Farmers can contact their local horticulture office for any queries related to the scheme. 

The contact details of the Department of Horticulture can be found on the official state government websites. 

The scheme also includes provisions for periodic evaluation and monitoring to assess its impact on farmers' livelihoods. 

Regular workshops and training sessions are organized to educate farmers about the latest horticultural practices. 

The government aims to establish at least 50,000 new orchards under this scheme by 2025. 

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities for around 1 million people in the horticulture sector. 

It also aims to enhance the availability of fresh fruits in local markets. 

The initiative aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to promote agricultural diversification and reduce dependency on traditional crops. 

Farmers are encouraged to cultivate a variety of fruits including mangoes, guavas, and citrus fruits. 

The scheme also promotes the use of organic farming techniques to ensure the sustainability of fruit production. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme provides access to quality planting material and technical expertise. 

The government collaborates with various agricultural universities and research institutions to provide farmers with the latest information on horticulture. 

The Naye Fal Bagicho Ki Sthapana scheme is expected to significantly contribute to the overall growth of the horticulture sector in India. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the successful implementation of this scheme over the next five years. 

This funding will be utilized for providing subsidies, training programs, and infrastructure development related to horticulture. 

The scheme also aims to promote the establishment of cold storage facilities to reduce post-harvest losses. 

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power in the market. 

The government provides support for the establishment of marketing facilities to help farmers sell their produce directly to consumers. 

The initiative is expected to improve the nutritional status of the population by increasing the availability of fruits. 

The scheme is also aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The government aims to ensure food security and improve the livelihoods of rural communities through this initiative. 

Overall, Naye Fal Bagicho Ki Sthapana represents a significant step towards enhancing the horticulture sector in India. 

It provides a comprehensive framework for supporting farmers in establishing new orchards and improving their income. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to promoting sustainable agriculture and improving the quality of life for farmers. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to enhance their agricultural practices and contribute to the economy. 

The success of the Naye Fal Bagicho Ki Sthapana scheme will depend on the active participation of farmers and the effective implementation by the government. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme to ensure that it meets its objectives and benefits the intended beneficiaries.
